 AMARILLO, Texas (KVII) — Before grabbing a quick breakfast from a vending machine or workplace cooler, Texas Panhandle residents may want to check the label.
 A nationwide food safety concern has reached Texas and Oklahoma, with federal officials warning that certain ready-to-eat biscuit products may be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes, a bacterium that can cause serious illness.
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service issued a public health alert Nov. 14 involving biscuit and sausage gravy meals distributed in six states, including Texas and Oklahoma.
 The warning has since expanded. Fresh & Ready Foods LLC, based in Longview, Texas, announced an expanded recall Nov. 17 involving breakfast sandwiches and biscuit-and-gravy meals made with potentially contaminated biscuits.
 The Food and Drug Administration published the expanded recall Nov. 18.
 What Texas Panhandle consumers should check 
 The affected products include: 
 Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy: 9.5-ounce packages with use-by dates Nov. 12-18, 2026, and establishment number EST. 51248.
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich: 5.7-ounce packages with expiration dates Nov. 12-22, 2026.
 The products were distributed through workplace break rooms, grab-and-go coolers, refrigerated vending machines and small self-service markets between Oct. 15 and Nov. 11.
 The biscuit-and-gravy meals were distributed in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Tennessee. The expanded sandwich recall also includes Alabama.
 Why Amarillo-area residents should pay attention 
 The distribution area includes two states served by the Amarillo television market: Texas and Oklahoma.
 That means consumers in Amarillo and surrounding Panhandle communities, as well as viewers in the Oklahoma Panhandle, should be aware of the warning, particularly if they purchase refrigerated breakfast meals at work.
 Federal officials have not identified specific Amarillo-area businesses or vending machine locations that received the products. Statewide distribution does not establish that the products were sold locally.
 How the contamination concern began 
 The expanded recall stems from biscuits supplied by C.H. Guenther & Son, a San Antonio-based company that recalled certain biscuit products because of possible listeria contamination.
 Fresh & Ready Foods used some of those biscuits in its prepared breakfast meals at its Longview facility.
 Federal officials said additional products could be identified as the investigation continues.
 What is listeria? 
 Listeria is a bacterium that can cause listeriosis, a potentially serious foodborne illness.
 Symptoms may include fever, muscle aches, headache, nausea and diarrhea. Severe infections can affect the nervous system.
 Pregnant women, newborns, adults 65 and older and people with weakened immune systems face a greater risk of serious complications. Infection during pregnancy can lead to miscarriage, stillbirth or serious illness in newborns.
 As of the company’s latest announcement, no illnesses had been reported in connection with the recalled products.
 What should consumers do?
 Consumers who have purchased the affected products should not eat them, even if the expiration date has passed. They should throw them away.
 Anyone experiencing symptoms or concerned about possible exposure should contact a health care provider.
 Fresh & Ready Foods is also offering information about refunds.
 Consumer contact information: 
 Phone: (855) 424-8390
 Email: RecallConcern@HotLineGlobal.com 
 Hours: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern time
 Consumers can view the affected product labels and photographs in the FDA’s official recall announcement .
 Federal food safety officials are urging consumers to continue checking for updates as the investigation into the recalled biscuits continues.
